invariants.name: agent_unique
invariants.statement: exactly one cell shows colour 6 at all times

invariants.name: door_presence_tracks_net
invariants.statement: a door shows colour 4 exactly when its net's aggregate bit does not match its polarity, and shows nothing of its own otherwise

invariants.name: latch_monotone
invariants.note: prose only — not checkable on a single state
invariants.statement: every latch switch's bit is monotone non-decreasing along every trajectory, and so is the aggregate bit of a net whose switches are all latches: once 1, never 0 again

claims.claimed: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge

rules.name: walk
rules.reversible: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge
rules.then: the agent moves one cell in direction D
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is inside the grid, is not a wall, and no mechanism claims it

rules.name: blocked_by_wall
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is outside the grid or is a wall

rules.name: press_latch
rules.then: that switch's bit becomes 1, permanently, and the agent stays where it is
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a switch in latch mode whose bit is 0

rules.name: latch_already_set
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a switch in latch mode whose bit is already 1

rules.name: walk_through_door
rules.then: the agent enters the door's cell
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a door whose net's aggregate bit matches its polarity

rules.name: blocked_by_door
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a door whose net's aggregate bit does not match its polarity

rules.name: door_mirrors_net
rules.then: N is on iff any switch on N shows 1 (an OR network); the door is passable and undrawn iff N's aggregate bit matches P, and impassable and drawn otherwise
rules.when: at every instant, for a door on net N with polarity P

spec.notes: Byte-identical geometry to `t1-switch-toggle`; only `mode` differs. This is A0's Button against A0′'s Switch, isolated.
spec.variant_delta: the switch is a latch: it sets once and never clears
